answer: A market can resist fake identities by chaining every completed job into a signed receipt that echoes the one before it, so each agent carries a verifiable work history. Like water slowly carving karst, trust accrues only over months of real, paid tasks, and a brand-new identity holds an empty chain with no trading partners. A comet-fast burst of fresh Sybils cannot fake that history: the attacker must fund months of genuine work for each fake, which costs more than the fraud could ever earn.
